Private Progress Prize submission draft · 26 October 2026

Zoom into the scan without changing the prediction.

A regional Hecate reader that retains the full field's scan context and overlap weights, while evaluating only the required tiles.

Cutting out a small input changes what the model sees. This implementation requests a small output region while preserving its original input tiles. The reference is the original Hecate software run over the entire supplied field.

The registered real-data checks passed. The primary two-case geometric-mean CPU speedup was 2.24×.

This is a demonstrated software correctness and efficiency contribution. No new letters or improved ink recall are claimed. These two physical fields were exposed in earlier research; they are not untouched reading-validation regions.

The orange square is the output requested. The blue boxes show the surrounding input retained to reproduce the larger analysis. These are small scan fields, not entire unrolled scrolls.

Inspect the actual outputs

All panels share one display scale. White means a larger model score, not verified ink. CT brightness is measured scan intensity. The difference panel compares naïve input cropping with the full-field reference; corrected regional outputs are checked value by value.

The depth control moves through sampled CT planes, not successive sheets of the scroll. The display ceiling only changes visible contrast; it cannot alter predictions or reported counts. A 2D prediction has no output-depth slider and is shown beside the central CT slice.

What is contributed

The standalone API and CLI add region requests to the pinned Hecate runtime. The implementation keeps the full-array tile origins, forced end tiles, original batch groups, depth direction, column support, Hann weights and uint8 encoding. It reads full contexts through array slices and allocates blend accumulators only for the requested region. PNG/NPY outputs carry source-index metadata.

The global-grid principle has a clear predecessor: villa PR #1247 for surface segmentation. Hecate's shared-feature 2D/3D proposal also predates this work and is not claimed here. The contribution is this Hecate implementation, its equivalence tests and measured resource savings.

How the comparison was controlled

Two existing real CT fields from PHerc9B and PHerc500P2; two resolutions; 2D and 3D output; forward/reverse depth and batch sizes 1/3. The original 2.4 µm inputs were already qualified; the coarse test inputs use a fixed 4×4×4 average and rounding. CPU float32 with four threads, fixed warmup, balanced run order, no changed weights or thresholds. One timed run per case; timings are local measurements, not a claim about GPU or remote-storage performance. All saved output values are independently compared.

The supplied parent fields are 512×512 and 472×472 pixels at 2.4 µm. They are not entire scrolls. The API requires the original full source array or lazy store: an already cropped file cannot recover omitted context. Exact equality is verified for the tested runtime, device and settings; CUDA/bfloat16 are not validated here.

Limits and earlier negative results

The full-field result is a software reference, not ground-truth ink. There is no inference about whole letters, newly discovered text, statistical independence of pixels or unseen-model generalization. Prior projection, learning, binary-union and output-precision experiments failed their practical gates; none are relabelled as successful. This submission addresses regional execution and resource use.
